browser.text: Firefox ESR runs on the club's server next to your box, and everything you open stays in its window: searches and every website. Your lab machine opens as http://target, a web server you start in your box as http://box:8000, and downloads land in your box's ~/Downloads. Ctrl+V pastes what you copied on your own computer, and what you copy in Firefox reaches your computer too. Websites see the club's server, not you, and the club keeps a list of the sites visited from the box.
browser.title: Firefox

burp.text: Open Burp Suite from its icon on the desktop or in the panel, or from the Applications menu behind the club's logo, top left. It runs on the club's server next to Firefox and opens as it does on Kali, in under a minute: the first time, PortSwigger's terms and conditions, which you read and accept to go on; then choose Temporary project in memory and Next, then Use Burp defaults and Start Burp. While Burp runs, everything Firefox opens on target or box passes through it: Proxy > HTTP history lists every request, Intercept holds one so that you can change it before it goes on, and Repeater sends one again as often as you like. Websites do not pass through Burp, and Burp can reach nothing that Firefox cannot. If you minimise Burp, click its empty screen to bring it back.
burp.title: Burp Suite

target.text: Start a lab's machine on its page, and it joins your box as "target": try nmap target, curl http://target or nc target 9001. The command target lists its open ports. Only your own machine is there: no other student, and not the server.
target.title: Your target

terminal.text: It works like Kali's terminal: Ctrl+Shift+C copies, Ctrl+Shift+V pastes and Ctrl+C stops the running command. Ctrl+Shift+T opens a tab, Ctrl+Shift+R and Ctrl+Shift+D split the window, Ctrl+Shift+F finds text, and Ctrl + and Ctrl - change the text size. Your browser keeps a few keys for itself (Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+Shift+W, Ctrl+Shift+N, Ctrl+PgUp, Ctrl+PgDn): press F11 for full screen and they reach the terminal too. Move a window by its title bar and resize it from any edge or corner.
terminal.title: Terminal

time.text: A box runs for two hours and can be extended in its last ten minutes. When it stops, everything in it is wiped: download what you want to keep.
time.title: Time

tools.text: Your box has the tools the labs call for: type tools in the terminal for the full list, by topic. They reach your lab machine, which answers as target. The box has no internet, so names such as google.com or any website do not resolve in it: that is on purpose, so that nobody attacks a real site from the club's server. Read up in Firefox instead. CyberChef and the picture viewer need no box. Start a machine on its lab page, then try these:
tools.title: Tools and commands
